# Paris Apartment Rental Preparation for a 9-Month Abroad Stay

A practical rental setup for a **2-bedroom, 68 m² apartment in Paris** while you are away from **2026-07-01 to 2027-03-31**. This is framed to help reduce **damage risk, late rent, and tenant disputes** without trying to give a legal ruling.

## Lease Review Checklist for a Safer Tenancy

- **Lease type and duration**
  - Confirm the rental form fits your plan for a fixed 9-month absence.
  - Check whether the lease can end cleanly on your return date or whether notice rules apply.

- **Rent payment terms**
  - State the exact due date, payment method, and account details.
  - Add a late-payment process: reminder timing, grace period if any, and escalation steps.

- **Security deposit**
  - Specify the deposit amount, when it is collected, and when it is returned.
  - Tie deductions to documented damage, unpaid rent, missing keys, or unpaid charges.

- **Condition of the apartment**
  - Attach a detailed inventory and move-in inspection as lease exhibits.
  - Make clear that the tenant receives the apartment in clean, functional condition.

- **Repairs and maintenance**
  - Separate tenant responsibility from owner responsibility.
  - Require prompt reporting of leaks, appliance failures, mold, lock issues, and water damage.

- **Use of the apartment**
  - Limit occupancy to approved residents only.
  - Prohibit subletting, unauthorized guests, and commercial use unless you allow them in writing.

- **Dispute handling**
  - Require written notice for complaints and repair requests.
  - Set a preferred communication channel and keep all key notices in writing.

- **Insurance**
  - Require tenant liability/home insurance proof before move-in and renewal proof during the lease.
  - Keep your own landlord coverage current as well.

- **Access and inspections**
  - Define notice rules before any owner access.
  - Reserve access for emergencies, repairs, and agreed inspection visits.

- **End-of-lease return**
  - State how the move-out inspection will be done.
  - Require all keys, badges, remotes, and manuals to be returned.

## Move-In Inspection and Document Pack

### Move-In Inspection Checklist
- **Entry and security**
  - Front door, locks, peephole, intercom, keys, mailbox access, window locks
- **Walls and surfaces**
  - Cracks, stains, holes, peeling paint, wall-mounted fixtures
- **Floors and ceilings**
  - Scratches, stains, tiles, loose boards, water marks
- **Kitchen**
  - Sink, taps, drainage, hob, oven, fridge, extractor, cabinets, smoke detector
- **Bathrooms**
  - Toilet, shower, bathtub, seals, ventilation, water pressure, leaks, mold
- **Bedrooms and living areas**
  - Windows, shutters, radiators, outlets, lighting, storage, curtains/blinds
- **Utilities and meters**
  - Electricity, gas, water meter readings, internet handoff, fuse box
- **Appliances and furnishings**
  - Test every included item and note brand, model, condition, and defects
- **Safety items**
  - Smoke alarms, carbon monoxide devices if present, fire extinguisher if provided
- **Shared areas**
  - Hallway, cellar, parking, bike storage, trash area, building access rules

### Recommended Move-In Evidence
- Date-stamped photos of every room, fixture, and existing defect
- Short video walkthrough from entry to exit
- Signed inventory of furnishings and appliances
- Meter readings taken on handover day
- Copies of all keys and access devices issued
- Tenant acknowledgment that they received the condition report

### Documents to Collect Before Handing Over
- Government ID and passport copy
- Proof of current address
- Proof of employment, contract, or income
- Recent payslips or bank statements
- Previous landlord reference, if available
- Tenant insurance certificate
- Signed lease and signed inventory/condition report
- Guarantor details, if you require one
- Contact details for emergency communication
- Consent for written notices by email and/or messaging, if appropriate

## Tenant Screening Workflow for Lower Risk

### 1) Set your minimum criteria
- Stable income relative to rent
- Clear identity and address history
- Ability to pay deposit and first month on time
- Acceptable references
- Willingness to provide insurance and sign inventory documents

### 2) Collect the same information from every applicant
- ID and contact details
- Employment and income proof
- Rental history
- Reason for moving
- Number of occupants
- Pets, smoking, and work-from-home use
- Desired move-in date and lease length

### 3) Verify the basics
- Match ID to the applicant
- Confirm income documents look consistent
- Call or email references
- Check prior landlord feedback on payment behavior, cleanliness, and communication
- Confirm the applicant understands the apartment rules

### 4) Compare applicants consistently
- Use the same scoring criteria for all candidates
- Prioritize payment reliability, reference quality, and clarity of communication
- Flag missing documents before moving forward

### 5) Finalize with written protections
- Collect deposit and first payment before handover
- Sign lease, inventory, and insurance proof
- Confirm move-in date, key handoff, and emergency contacts
- Store all documents in one shared folder

## Practical Risk-Reduction Plan Before You Leave

- Appoint a local contact in Paris for emergencies and repairs
- Keep a complete digital file with lease, photos, inventory, and receipts
- Use written communication for rent reminders, approvals, and repair requests
- Schedule a mid-term check-in if the lease and tenant relationship allow it
- Keep a move-out inspection date penciled in well before your return

## Quick Actions
